description:
Redwood Inference is launching a structured case study + customer reference program to recruit 3–5 design partners willing to participate in (1) public case studies and (2) scheduled reference calls for qualified prospects. The program supports Redwood’s PLG-to-sales-assisted motion by providing credible proof of production outcomes (latency, cost/token, reliability, deployment flexibility) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Recruit and secure written approval from 3–5 customers to publish a public case study (web + PDF) with quantified outcomes and architectural details.
- Establish an internal, repeatable reference process: intake, qualification, scheduling, prep, and post-call follow-up.
- Arm Sales/CS with reusable assets (talk tracks, objection handling, security FAQ snippets) and a single source of truth for reference availability.

Scope (in-scope):
- Target account selection (ICP + prioritization), outreach, and executive alignment.
- Legal/comms workflow: NDA considerations, customer quote/logo releases, and final approval checkpoints.
- Case study production: interview plan, metrics validation, narrative drafting, design, publishing, and enablement rollout.
- Reference call operations: request intake form, routing rules, prep docs, scheduling cadence, and feedback loop.

Out of scope:
- Broad brand campaign, paid media, or major website redesign beyond a case-studies section update.
- Deep product changes unrelated to enabling customer proofs (minor doc/site updates are allowed).

Primary stakeholders:
- Executive sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO)
- Marketing: Camila Reyes (VP Marketing), Soojin Lee (Dir Product Marketing), Ben Carter (Growth)
- Sales: Stephanie Nguyen (VP Sales NA), Lukas Meyer (VP Sales EMEA), AEs (Avery Johnson, Priyom Das, Hannah Schmitt)
- Customer Success: Jasmine Liu (VP CS), Rachel Kim (Dir CS Enterprise), Miguel Santos (Sr CSM)
- Solutions Engineering: Markus Klein (Dir SE), Simran Kaur (Solutions Architect)
- Legal: Michael Grant (GC), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel)

Proposed timeline (8–10 weeks):
- Weeks 1–2: Program definition (templates, legal workflow), target list, outreach plan, tracking in HubSpot.
- Weeks 3–5: Customer recruitment + kickoff interviews; validate metrics and deployment details.
- Weeks 6–8: Draft case studies, internal review, customer review/redlines, design + web publishing.
- Weeks 9–10: Reference call program goes live; sales enablement rollout; post-launch retrospective and pipeline impact review.

Constraints and considerations:
- Customer confidentiality and procurement/legal requirements (logo/quote approval, security language).
- Accuracy of performance and cost metrics; require validation and reproducible measurement notes.
- Avoid overpromising; ensure claims map to documented capabilities and current SLAs.

Key deliverables:
- Reference program playbook + intake/scheduling workflow.
- Case study template pack (interview guide, metrics checklist, approval checklist).
- 3–5 published case studies + internal reference profiles.
- CRM tracking (HubSpot activity timeline, reference readiness fields, owner routing).
- Enablement: talk track, discovery questions, and standard reference request process.

files.description: Program charter and operating model: goals, eligibility criteria, roles (AE/CSM/SE/Marketing/Legal), reference call routing rules, SLAs for scheduling, and governance (who approves what).
Standard case study structure (problem, constraints, architecture, implementation, measurable outcomes), writing guidelines, required data points, and examples of acceptable claims/metrics phrasing.

Interview script and question bank for engineering + business stakeholders, including prompts for latency/cost baselines, reliability incidents, deployment/security constraints, and decision rationale (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
Step-by-step approval flow: quote verification, logo usage, security language review, final sign-off path, and required artifacts (release form, approvals in email/Drive).
Legal process for customer-facing marketing: standard release language options, handling NDAs/MSAs, redline guidance, and escalation criteria to GC for sensitive accounts.
Reusable template for a customer quote/logo release (fields for company, approved quotes, spokesperson name/title, approved claims, and term/withdrawal language).
Messaging framework mapping Redwood differentiators (throughput/latency, cost controls, reliability/fallbacks, deployment flexibility) to recommended case study angles and proof points.
CS playbook for reference readiness: ensuring stable production usage, identifying champions, setting expectations for reference calls, and collecting ongoing outcomes for future updates.
Working project plan: milestones, owners, dependencies, weekly checklist, and risks (legal delays, metrics validation, customer bandwidth).
Spreadsheet-style tracker of target accounts with ICP fit, product usage, champion strength, deployment mode, status (contacted/interviewed/approved), and next steps.
Draft outbound/inbound follow-up copy for AEs/CSMs, including asks for public case study participation, reference calls, and approval steps.
Table of proposed metrics per customer (latency p50/p95, cost/token, error rates, throughput) with data sources, measurement windows, and validation owner (SE/CS).
Outline and rough narrative for Arcadia Health (regulated workload, VPC/Private constraints), including architecture sketch notes and candidate quotes.
Outline and rough narrative for QuantaPay (fintech, Dedicated capacity, strict latency SLOs), including baseline vs post-Redwood metrics placeholders.
Outline and rough narrative for NovaDocs (SaaS doc search/embeddings + reranking), including cost optimization and caching/batching notes.
Internal prep sheet template for reference calls: prospect context, do/don’t topics, product areas to highlight, and backup SE attendee guidance.
Rolling log of internal edits and customer feedback/redlines by section (claims, security language, metrics wording) with resolution status.
HubSpot company record for Arcadia Health: stage, owners (AE/SE/CSM), deployment requirements (VPC/Private), security requirements, activity timeline, blockers, and reference readiness status.
HubSpot company record for QuantaPay: Dedicated evaluation notes, latency/throughput targets, procurement checklist, and tracking for case study + reference consent.
HubSpot company record for NovaDocs: Hosted API + Optimize adoption notes, cost sensitivity, and planned publish window for a performance/cost case study.
HubSpot company record for HelioSupport: support-agent use case, routing/fallback requirements, and candidate champions for reference calls.
HubSpot company record for VectorForge: developer tools/code-assistant workload, preference for open models, and requirements for structured output/function calling.
HubSpot company record for Moonlake Insurance (backup candidate): early security review notes, data residency concerns, and risk assessment for public logo/quotes.
HubSpot company record for GlassKite AI (backup candidate): fast-moving startup, strong PLG usage, but uncertain willingness for public case study—tracked as ‘maybe’.

Security/compliance review transcript: SOC 2 evidence requests, KMS/key ownership, audit logging expectations, and how public case study language must avoid sensitive details.
Reference program kickoff transcript: confirms spokesperson, approval workflow, interview schedule, and metrics Redwood can publish.
Demo transcript: Dedicated capacity, Console dashboards, rollout/fallback policies; prospect asks about predictable latency and burst behavior.
POC scoping transcript: benchmarking plan, traffic replay approach, acceptance thresholds, and agreement to participate in a case study if targets are met.
Weekly POC check-in transcript: early results, issues encountered, and discussion of how to phrase measurable outcomes for publication.
Discovery transcript: embeddings + reranking workload, cost concerns, caching/batching discussion, and content marketing interest (public architecture diagram).
Technical deep dive transcript: Optimize recommendations, model versioning/rollouts, and how to calculate and validate cost-per-query improvements.
POC scoping transcript: support-agent latency targets, streaming stability needs, fallback policies, and reference call expectations.
POC check-in transcript: troubleshooting timeouts/429s, action items for rate limits, and alignment on what can be shared publicly.
Discovery transcript: code-assistant workload, structured output needs, open model preferences, and interest in a performance-focused story.
Demo transcript: SDK integration, streaming/tool calling patterns, and discussion of what engineering details are acceptable in a public write-up.
Partner coordination transcript: aligning a joint announcement angle (marketplace listing + customer story), approval timelines, and asset requirements.
